chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Hammam, who said: Ahmad ibn Bundar narrated to us from Mansur ibn al-Abbas, from Ja'far al-Jawhari, from Zakariyya ibn Adam al-Qummi, from al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:
"Indeed, Allah saved Baghdad because of the location of the two tombs of the Al-Husayns within it."

key_terms.الرِّضَا: al-Rida (Imam Musa al-Kadhim's son, often used for Imam Ali al-Rida)
key_terms.قُبُورِ الْحُسَيْنِيَّيْنِ: the two tombs of the Al-Husayns

ai.seo_question: Why was Baghdad saved according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) attributes the preservation of Baghdad from divine calamities to the presence of the tombs of the two Al-Husayns, specifically referring to Imam al-Husayn (AS) and his son Ali ibn Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin), whose shrines are located in the city. This narration underscores the Shia belief in the intercessory power and spiritual barakah of the Ahl al-Bayt's resting places, serving as a source of protection and mercy for the communities that honor them.
